newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares soar to record on fresh capital.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares soar to record on fresh capital.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange maintained its record breaking form on Tuesday and closed at the third successive record high as fresh capital reached the market. But traders said they expected a slowdown to come.
The BUX index finished unofficially at 6,252.91 points, up 113.82 points or 1.85 percent, below a new trading peak of 6,278.45 points.

"Buyers' momentum is starting to run out of steam...the pace of the rise is going to slow down," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities. "Optimism has faded on the futures market with the June BUX falling below the spot index."
The last June BUX futures deal was made at 6,220 points.
Another trader said that foreigners who are generally main players on the market, were mostly buyers, benefiting from a strong dollar which maker Hungarian papers relatively cheap.
"A general buying mood prevails on the market," said Zsolt Madacsi of ING Barings. "The dollar is very strong, the forint is very weak and shares are very cheap for foreigners."
The trader said the fact that the index was above 6,000 was a psychological plus but he added that a correction would necessarily follow, "but not now".
Analysts said that fresh money was coming into the market from U.S. mutual funds and from investors switching to Hungary or Poland from the troubled Czech market.

"Most of the increases in the (Hungarian) stock market are due more to foreign money beating up prices," said Sara Zervos, emerging market strategist at BZW in London. "We haven't seen any big changes on the fundamentals front," she added. "We tend to think that it is a case of extra foreign money coming in."
"However, we do expect the economic situation in Hungary to be on an improving path which would suggest better fundamentals in which case we don't see a big decline coming up for Hungary," she said.

On Tuesday tile manufacturer Zalakeramia Rt was among the day's strong gainers, adding 245 forints to finish at 7,645, after it had acquired the purchase of a 62 percent stake in Romania's Cesarom via its Austrian subsidiary. "Zalakeramia rallied on the news of the acquisition," Nagy said.

Pharmaceuticals rallied with Richter Gedeon Rt surging to a new record of 15,800 forints, while Human benefited from the bullish market sentiment, coupled with a positive brokerage rating on Monday, traders said.
Human finished at 3,050 forints, up 130. "There were lots of sellers above 3,100 forints locking in profits," Nagy said.

Tuesday's record breakers included plastics products maker Pannonplast which rallied to 9,200 forints before ending at 9,151 forints, up 151 and chemicals BorsodChem which soared to 7,205 before closing at 7,135, up 180.
